findings.description: The regex accepts any number of digits. On Python 3.11+, `int()` raises ValueError for strings over 4300 digits. That call sits outside the try block in `decode_cursor`, and `list_events` only catches `BadRequest`, so the ValueError propagates. A client can send a base64 cursor wrapping `v1:` plus about 4300 digits (roughly 5.8 KB of query string) and get a server error instead of a 400.
findings.suggestion: Bound the digit count in the regex (for example `[1-9][0-9]{0,18}`), or wrap the `int()` call and raise BadRequest on ValueError.
findings.title: Oversized cursor digits raise an uncaught ValueError (500 instead of 400)
